performer.name: The Invitation
performer.stance: frazzled amateur organizer with a staple gun; talks fast, apologises a lot, keeps going anyway

structure: one week told in order: Wednesday night flyers, knocking on doors, Saturday at the bench, the notebook afterwards, the price, nobody claps
synopsis: A spoken-word number from a card deck about protopia: the future as slow, small improvement people take part in. A performer tells how they organised a first small repair job in their street, from putting up flyers to the first Saturday.
bestOfReason: Night of the flyers 3, 1, 2, 17: the ugly flyer, the open page, pencil, and the performer's own card naming time, place, task.
Doors 26, 27, 13, 15, 28: the first hello, the door that stays shut, the badly dressed neighbour who knows how, going first.
Saturday 19, 5, 6, 18, 7, 8: the clumsy start, one fixable thing, a repair not a revolution, shared hands, a boring win that compounds.
Afterwards 9, 33, 34: one breath against the feed, your own notes, the honest count.
Sneaking it in 42, 43: the tiny pilot stripe, mild disobedience.
Price and close 46, 47, 55, 56: trading certainty for agency, showing up again, nobody claps, pick up the pencil.

omitted.10-12: body and attention cards; 9 carries the one breath
omitted.21-24: present-tense cards; the week itself is told in the present
omitted.48: refers to the other two decks' bargain
omitted.49-54: design-signature cards; 56 lands the pencil instead

orderReason: Cards follow one week in time instead of deck order: the flyer (3) before the idea on it (1, 2); the performer's own card (17) closes the flyer night; door cards before the Saturday cards; 9 moves to the moment someone checks the news during the repair.

cues.cue: staple gun clacks on the backbeat
street noise, a bus pulls away

beats: Wednesday, eleven at night, one staple gun, two hundred flyers. If you walked home tonight, you've seen one. Sorry about your lamppost.
Nobody is coming to save us. Nobody is coming to doom us either. Some people call what's left protopia. I call it Saturday.

beats.pre: Yes, I made the flyer myself.
beats.text: The Ugly First Draft: make the first version bad on purpose. Bad is how you know it is real.
The Open Notebook: the future is a process of slow, incremental improvement you participate in.
The Erasable Line: draw the next step in pencil; you expect to be wrong and stay anyway.
The Invitation: turn watching into showing up. Name a time, a place, a task.
beats.post: Saturday, nine, the bench by the bus stop. Bring gloves.

beats: Thursday I did the doors. Every door on the street.

beats.text: The First Hello: lower the bar to contact. Most cooperation starts embarrassingly small.
The Risk of Being Soft-Blocked: they might not respond. Your nervous system thinks that is death. It is not.

beats.pre: Third door, a man holding a wrench.
beats.text: The Person Nearby: authority is overrated, proximity is underrated. Ask the one who does the thing.
The Unimpressive Source: real know-how is often badly dressed and lives three doors down.

beats.pre: After that, I knocked first everywhere.
beats.text: The Widened Circle: go first. Every ally was a stranger until somebody did.

beats: Saturday, nine. Four of them came. Last time it was me and a thermos, so this is a movement.

beats.text: The Awkward Start: go to the first small, clumsy gathering anyway. Clumsy is the entry fee.

beats.pre: The bench has a loose slat.
beats.text: The Fixable Thing: one broken thing close enough to touch. A specific, local, finishable task.
The Right-Sized Move: choose a repair you can finish this week, not a revolution you can only announce.
The Shared Hands: mutual aid is older than money. Split a problem the way your ancestors raised a barn.

beats.pre: Somebody checks the news halfway through. Wait.
beats.text: The Held Breath: before reacting, take the one breath the feed is built to deny you.
The Boring Win: repair is undervalued because it is undramatic. Small fixes do not trend.

beats.pre: Next week, the hinge on the hall.
beats.text: The Compounding: one repair a week is fifty-two a year. Nobody clapped, and the place is different.

beats: Sunday I wrote it all down.

beats.text: The Logged Observation: write down what you actually saw, not what the headline said you would see.
The Honest Denominator: count the whole thing, including the times it worked and nobody noticed.

beats: Between us, about the corner by the school.

beats.pre: That little white stripe on the crossing?
beats.text: The Pilot Move: run a tiny version. Low stakes, real feedback, no permission needed.
The Quiet Sabotage: improvement often looks like mild disobedience to a stuck system.
The Comfort of Maybe: trade the warm baths of hopeless and handled for the cold shower of it depends on us.
The Ongoing Effort: there is no final version. The cost is showing up again next week.
The Quiet Start: nobody will clap. Start anyway. The clapping was never the point.
The Core Question: forget the brochure. Ignore the loop. Pick up the pencil.

beats: Doom gets the subscriptions. Rescue gets the tickets. A Saturday with a loose slat earns nothing, which is how you know it's yours.
Same bench, next week, nine. Bring gloves.
